---
title: "Earth2Studio.jl"
---

Welcome to the documentation for **Earth2Studio.jl**.

## Overview

Earth2Studio.jl is a Julia wrapper around [NVIDIA's earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) Python package for AI-powered weather and climate forecasting. It provides:

- **Data Sources**: Access ERA5 reanalysis, GFS forecasts, HRRR, and more via a unified interface.
- **Prognostic Models**: Run state-of-the-art AI weather models including FourCastNet, Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, Aurora, and AIFS.
- **Diagnostic Models**: Apply downscaling (CorrDiff), precipitation estimation, tropical cyclone tracking, and derived quantities.
- **Ensemble Forecasting**: Generate perturbed ensemble members with Gaussian, bred vector, and lagged ensemble methods.
- **Verification Metrics**: Compute RMSE, ACC, CRPS, Brier scores, and more.

The package uses [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl) and [CondaPkg.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/CondaPkg.jl) to manage the Python environment automatically.

## Quickstart

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/RallypointOne/Earth2Studio.jl")
```

The base package installs lightweight Python dependencies (numpy, xarray). To use AI models, add `earth2studio` with the desired extras to your project's `CondaPkg.toml`:

```toml
[pip.deps]
"earth2studio[pangu]" = ""
```

Then run a deterministic forecast:

```julia
using Earth2Studio
using Dates

# Load data and model
data = GFS()
model = Pangu24()
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")

# Run a 10-step forecast from a specific date
result = run_deterministic(DateTime(2024, 1, 15), 10, model, data, io)

# Convert results to Julia arrays
ds = to_xarray(result)
```
